title: In vino veritas
summary: "In Vino Veritas" is a section of Søren Kierkegaard's Stages on Life's Way, a work published under pseudonyms and assembled from several voices. Written as a modern companion to Plato's Symposium, it is framed as a recollection by the pseudonymous narrator William Afham. A group of friends, including Constantin Constantius, the Young Man, Victor Eremita, a Fashion Designer and Johannes the Seducer, gathers for a banquet at which each guest must give a speech on erotic love after drinking wine. Each speaker treats love from a different angle: as comic and unexplainable, as a matter of amusement and irony, as a folly of vanity, or as a life of seduction without substance. The section closes with a glimpse of a married couple in a garden, suggesting that love can work despite its absurdity. The piece is a study of the aesthetic life and its limits, and it ends by pointing toward a Christian understanding of love as grounded in divine love. The text here is a reader's essay about the work rather than Kierkegaard's own words.
